output.brief: The enrolment drop is mostly a yield problem, not an Admissions Office failure. Applications and admits rose, so the applicant pool is not the cause. Yield fell only in the two tiers whose scholarships were cut: Dean's awards went from $14,000 to $9,000 and Merit awards from $9,000 to $5,000. Yield was flat for Presidential awards, which were unchanged, and for students with no merit award. Early-action students had their decisions on the old timetable and the old system, yet their yield fell by about the same amount as regular-decision yield (7.4 against 7.5 points). That points to the scholarship change rather than the slow portal. The slow regular-decision turnaround was real and probably cost some individual students, but the evidence doesn't show it drove the overall drop. I'm fairly confident in this. I did not test whether the portal lost documents, and I couldn't separate the effect of the frozen reader posts from the portal's scoring module. Recommendations: do not replace the director on this basis. Take the award schedule back to the finance committee, with the net-revenue trade-off modelled for the Dean's and Merit tiers, before award letters go out. Set a monthly decision-turnaround target as a secondary step. Hold off on ordering a rebuild of the upload module until the missing-document problem is verified.
